title: 식당에서 반찬 더 달라고 하기: "김치 좀 더 주세요"
objective: You can politely ask for more side dishes and use -을까요/-ㄹ까요 to make an offer or a suggestion.
summary: Learn how to call the staff and ask for more side dishes at a Korean restaurant.
setting: Lunchtime at a small Korean restaurant (a 백반집 with many side dishes). Two friends are eating. One of them calls the staff to ask for more side dishes.

task.title: Ask for more side dishes
task.line: Use the dialogue and the word list to choose, fill in, build, or answer in Korean.

words.exampleMeaning: Excuse me, could I get some water?
This place has tasty side dishes.

words.meaning: a word that makes a request softer, like 'please'

words.exampleMeaning: Shall I bring you some small plates?

words.meaning: Is it possible? / Is that OK?
words.exampleMeaning: Can I get it to go?
Please give me the sauce on the side.

dialogue.meaning: Could I have some more kimchi, please?
Sure. Shall I bring more bean sprouts too?

dialogue.korean: 네, 좋아요. 그리고 계란말이도 더 돼요?
dialogue.meaning: Yes, please. And can I get more rolled omelet too?
Sorry. Please order the rolled omelet separately.
Then shall we order one rolled omelet?

dialogue.korean: 네. 반찬은 저쪽 셀프 코너에도 있어요.
dialogue.meaning: Okay. There are side dishes at the self-service corner over there, too.

exercises: Choose the right word (좀 / 따로): 저기요, 단무지 ____ 더 주세요.
Add -을까요 after a consonant or -ㄹ까요 after a vowel: ① 우리 떡볶이 ____? (먹다) ② 우리 비빔밥 ____? (시키다)
Read the dialogue and answer Yes or No: Can the customer get more 계란말이 as an extra side dish, like the kimchi?
Fill in the blank with a word from the word list: 반찬은 ____예요. 저기에서 가져가세요.
Put the words in order to make a request: 주세요 / 좀 / 깍두기 / 더
